Last year, after a some resistance, we agreed to do a secret santa and it went pretty well. Or so I thought. This year 1 sibling threw a fit about doing it. She said she doesn't like "putting rules on holidays" and it's not fair. As a side note, she and our younger siblings rarely buy anyone anything. Last year was the 1st time everyone brought something. Another sibling, who is hosting Christmas, sided with her and said that we won't do a secret Santa but that you don't have to bring gifts if you don't want to. Am an asshole if I don't buy my siblings gifts? I love my family but I can't afford it this year. I was going to get nieces and nephews gifts but that's it.

Now, I'm feeling pressured because if I don't buy gifts for my siblings, am I being a bad person? I love my family, but I can't afford it this year. Next, the emotional aspect. I love my family, and I don't want them to feel neglected. But if I can't afford to buy gifts for everyone, how can I show my love without spending too much? I should also consider the teachings of Islam regarding family and charity. If I can't afford it, it's not a failing on my part but a responsible decision. Finding a balance that respects everyone's feelings and circumstances is key.
